The purpose and interaction of `scripts/dev/sync_fix_impact.py` with the orchestrator are not described in the design, despite being listed as an affected file.

The API contract for `/api/v1/health` specifies `auth: none`. For an enterprise system, even health endpoints can benefit from basic authentication or network-level controls, and this inconsistency with other authenticated endpoints should be justified.
BLOCKER: The "Enterprise Autonomous Gate Orchestrator" is implemented in Python (`scripts/dev/gate_orchestrator.py`) and serves as the runtime entrypoint for core pipeline orchestration. This violates the "new shipped logic -> Go" standard for a core enterprise component, despite the prior disposition classifying it as "tooling".

MAJOR: The `precheck.py` script now defaults `PF_BACKLOG_DB` to "on" if unset, shifting its default operational mode from file-based to DB-based. This change, while aligning with the global `PF_BACKLOG_DB` default, may cause unexpected failures in local development or CI environments not configured for a DB-backed backlog. This impacts maintainability and developer experience.

NIT: The `rollback` entry is duplicated in `functional_spec` and `design_pack`.
The `controls` and `implementation_controls` sections are identical, leading to redundancy.

The consistent use of `RollbackOrchestrator` in control symbols (e.g., `RollbackOrchestrator.verify_security_auth`) for an "Enterprise Autonomous Gate Orchestrator" suggests a potential naming mismatch, impacting clarity.
MAJOR: The design does not sufficiently detail how the Python script-based orchestrator achieves high availability, fault tolerance, or horizontal scalability for an "Enterprise Autonomous Gate Orchestrator." The claim of "Horizontally capable" is not supported by the described deployment model.

The rollback strategy for state changes made by the orchestrator in autonomous mode is insufficiently detailed beyond code reversion. It does not cover clean state restoration across multiple gates and external systems.

The `PF_BACKLOG_DB` configuration contract specifies `invalid_behavior: defaults to on`. This can silently enable the database even with invalid configuration, masking errors and potentially leading to runtime failures if the DB is unavailable.

The design implies `core/id_allocator.py` (Python) interacts with the Go `edpsvc` using an "authenticated bearer token." The secure handling and usage of this token by the Python component, especially concerning `CL-005` ("No PF token for internal callers"), is not explicitly detailed.
MINOR: The "Enterprise Autonomous Gate Orchestrator" remains located in `scripts/dev/gate_orchestrator.py`, which is misleading for a core, production-grade component and impacts maintainability. The prior disposition claiming this was addressed is incorrect.
The purpose and interaction of `scripts/dev/sync_fix_impact.py` with the orchestrator are not described in the design, despite being listed as an affected file.

The API contract for `/api/v1/health` specifies `auth: none`. For an enterprise system, this inconsistency with other authenticated endpoints should be justified or secured. The prior disposition claiming this was addressed is incorrect.
The design lacks specific observability details for the `core/id_allocator.py` component, which is critical for diagnosing potential data corruption or concurrency issues.

The security control `CTRL-01` (tenant isolation and authentication on post-deploy smoke probe execution) is linked to `AC-1` (Interactive HIL mode), which is an unclear and potentially misaligned association.

The tenant isolation control `CTRL-06` (rollback operation restores state cleanly without crossing tenant boundaries) is linked to `AC-2` (Autonomous mode auto-evaluation), which is not immediately obvious and could be more clearly articulated.
`scripts/dev/precheck.py` is a dependency for the core pipeline orchestration, but its enterprise readiness (stability, performance, standards adherence) is not elaborated.
BLOCKER: The "Enterprise Autonomous Gate Orchestrator" (`scripts/dev/gate_orchestrator.py`) is implemented in Python as the runtime entrypoint for new core pipeline orchestration, violating the "new shipped logic -> Go" standard. The prior disposition claiming this was addressed is incorrect.

The design lacks an explicit dry-run or report mode for autonomous operations, which is critical for blast radius control and integrity in an enterprise system. The prior disposition claiming this was addressed is incorrect.

requirements.title: Interactive HIL mode halts at review gates awaiting operator decision
inputs: Item ID, gate name, review findings
outputs: Interactive terminal prompt and operator decision
requirements.trigger: Execution of gate orchestrator in interactive mode
acceptance: Given interactive mode, When a review gate is encountered, Then execution halts and prompts operator for explicit sign-off.
data_rules: Strict interactive prompt when mode is interactive
edge_cases: Non-TTY terminal halts with clear prompt error
requirements.idempotency: Re-prompting without state mutation is idempotent
preconditions: Item in progress with gate review pending

requirements.title: Autonomous mode auto-evaluates dispositions and advances gates
outputs: Recorded dispositions and advanced gate state
requirements.trigger: Execution of gate orchestrator with --mode auto or PF_EXECUTION_MODE=auto
acceptance: Given auto mode with advisory findings, When gates execute, Then dispositions are auto-recorded and gates advance automatically.
data_rules: Blocking findings fail closed and halt auto mode
edge_cases: Fatal blocking finding stops auto mode and alerts operator
preconditions: Item in progress with advisory findings only

requirements.title: Execution mode resolver determines policy from item and environment
inputs: Item execution_mode field, PF_EXECUTION_MODE env var, CLI flag
acceptance: Given varying configuration levels, When mode is resolved, Then precedence hierarchy evaluates with safe interactive default.
data_rules: CLI flag > item field > env var > default INTERACTIVE
edge_cases: Unrecognized mode string safely defaults to INTERACTIVE
preconditions: Backlog item or environment configuration present

requirements.title: End-to-end pipeline gate orchestration and PostgreSQL DB authority
outputs: Gate 0 -> Gate 1.5 -> Gate 1 -> Gate 2.5 -> Gate 2 execution trail
acceptance: Given complete pipeline run, When all gates pass, Then delivery provenance and execution trail are stamped in DB and committed.
data_rules: PF_BACKLOG_DB defaults to 'on' everywhere without downgrade
edge_cases: Database retry on transient failure avoids data corruption
requirements.idempotency: Pipeline steps are re-entrant and record audit trail
preconditions: Backlog database running and schema initialized

observability: Structured JSON disposition logs and milestone audit trail events
data_lifecycle: Append-only execution trail persisted in engineering/trails/<ID>.json
open_questions: None - all architectural assumptions validated with operator.

config_contract.name: PF_EXECUTION_MODE
config_contract.precedence: cli flag > item field > env > default

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Interactive HIL mode prompts operator and halts at review gates (Gate 1 and Gate 2) awaiting explicit decision.
AC-2: Autonomous mode executes full review gate sequence automatically, auto-applying dispositions and advancing gates.
AC-3: Backlog execution mode resolver correctly determines mode from item execution_mode field or PF_GATE_MODE environment variable.
AC-4: Complete pipeline orchestration integrates gate0 -> gate1.5 -> gate1 -> tests -> gate2.5 -> gate2 -> precheck -> delivery.
